findings.title: Materials' 110% growth bet is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.66x forward versus 34.94x trailing, a 52 percent compression that implies 110 percent earnings growth. That is the largest implied growth in the table, yet the forward multiple sits at percentile 28 — the market is pricing a massive rebound without paying up for it.

findings.title: Energy's forward lens is far cheaper
findings.body: Energy's trailing P/E is at percentile 84 while its forward P/E sits at percentile 38, a 45-point gap — the widest in either direction outside Materials. The market is effectively discounting a 63 percent earnings jump, but the forward multiple's mid-range percentile suggests analysts see this as a cyclical peak, not a durable expansion.

findings.title: Health Care's forward multiple is maxed
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is at percentile 100, its richest level in five years, after a 13-point one-month jump. The 47 percent compression from trailing earnings implies 87 percent growth, but the percentile ceiling means there is no historical room left for the multiple to stretch further — only earnings can justify the price.
